newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Great Central raises gold estimate.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Great Central raises gold estimate.

text.p: Great Central Mines Ltd, part of the Joseph Gutnick mining group, said on Friday it had increased its proved and probable gold reserves in the June quarter by 2.37 million ounces to 4.87 million ounces.

The company, whose Jundee Barton Deeps and Bronzewing operations are based in Western Australia, said the higher reserve estimate was based on 32.7 million tonnes of ore grading 4.6 grams per tonne of gold.
It said the latest proved and probable reserves at Jundee Barton Deeps were 6.28 million tonnes at 9.0 g/t for 1.8 million ounces of gold. Other Jundee and stockpile reserves were 674,000 ounces.
Underground development at Jundee Barton Deeps was due to begin in August 1997 with production starting in February 1998.
Total reserves at Bronzewing were 2.385 million ounces.
Production for the quarter was 106,981 ounces at an average cash operating cost of A$293 an ounce.
This compared with production of 92,577 ounces at an operating cost of A$310 an ounce in the year earlier period.
Production for the year to June 30 was 436,209 ounces at an average cash operating price of A$277 an ounce. The average selling price for the June quarter was A$586 an ounce.
The company said current hedging and commitments including flat forwards and call and put options amounted to 2,005,671 ounces at an average price of A$607.

Great Central said results from drilling at Jundee Barton Deeps, which have not been included in the reserves estimate, continued to intersect significant mineralisation with results such as 13 metres at 37.2 grammes per tonne from a depth of 298 metres and 28 metres at 7.2 g/t from a depth of 179 metres.

"Other drilling at Jundee also continues to intersect structurally controlled high grade gold mineralisation including 38 metres at 18 g/t gold from a depth of 237 meters in the area between the Northwest and Barton pits," the company said.

"The company's high grade reserves, low cash operating costs and hedging programme have established the sold foundation for he company to continue to be a significant, profitable gold company in the long term," Great Central said.
Great Central shares were up a cent at A$2.50 at 12.45 p.m. (0244 GMT).
